newsitem.title: USA: Scientologists maintain campaign against Germany.
newsitem.headline: Scientologists maintain campaign against Germany.

text.p: German Scientologists who have left their country because of discrimination have formed a coalition to campaign against alleged human rights abuses in Germany, the Church of Scientology said on Monday.

It said the Alliance for Liberty and Rights of Minorities (ALARM) coalition, formed as a response to German's "fanatical policy of discrimination against Scientologists," represented Scientologists in the United States, Britain and Denmark.

Germany and the Los Angeles-based church have been engaged in a fierce war of words over the last few months. Scientology has compared Germany's treatment of its members to Nazi persecution of the Jews before the Second World War.
Germany does not accord Scientology the status of a religion, believing it to be a purely economic organisation.

In a press statement the church said hundreds of cases of discrimination against Scientologists in Germany existed. It said 600 of the cases were included in a complaint filed last month with the European Commission of Human Rights.

The statement did not say how many members the newly formed coalition had. It said the group planned to inform world leaders and the public about "discrimination and human rights abuses occurring against Scientologists in Germany."
